newsitem.title: FINLAND: Late spurt helps Helsinki back to neutral close.
newsitem.headline: Late spurt helps Helsinki back to neutral close.

text.p: Shares closed a mixed session flat on Tuesday, recovering on a late spurt of buying as foreign investors got into the market, brokers said.

The FOX stock futures index ended up 0.19 percent at 1,073.61, while the all-share HEX closed down 0.05 percent at 3,109.54 points. Decliners beat advancers 45 to 39. Volume was at summertime levels, amounting to just 433 million markka.
"This has been fairly neutral," one broker said, "the weather is beautiful, so there's already a bit of summer stagnation."
But a higher opening by Wall Street stocks boosted confidence at the close. "If the U.S. market holds up, we could rise quite nicely tomorrow," one broker said.
Telecom share Nokia ended down 2.00 markka at 352.00, but struggled back from an intraday low of 350.00 in fair 100 million markka volume.

Food packaging and confectionery group Huhtamaki added 2.00 markka to end at 225.00 after reporting January-April profits broadly in line with analysts' forecasts. Volume in the share was a modest 1.4 million markka.
But some brokers said they wanted to see better results from Huhtamaki. "It is an eternal promise, the whole company," one said.

Forestry group UPM-Kymmene ended 1.50 markka higher at 121.00 after lively 50 million markka dealings. Brokers said an announcement from UPM that it was in talks to buy U.S. Daubert Coated Products added interest in the share late in the day.

Software and systems group TT Tieto rose 26.00 markka to 444.00 in sturdy 14 million markka trade. Brokers said it was correcting from a fall which began in mid-May after it hit a 470.00 markka life high.
Bourse newcomer Kyro fell 1.10 markka to 37.30 after its strong debut on Monday. But it kept most of the gains built on top of its offering price of 27.00 per share.
Tyre maker Nokian Renkaat ended 2.00 markka lower at 138.00 after big in-house deals matched by Enskilda Securities at 138.00 and 139.00 markka.

A stream of interim reports from several big companies, including oil and energy group Neste, steel group Rautaruukki, engineering group Metra, and retail group Kesko, would set the pace on Wednesday, brokers said.
